newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Caltex Philippines crude unit shut for maintenance.
newsitem.headline: Caltex Philippines crude unit shut for maintenance.

text.p: Caltex (Phils) Inc, a unit of the joint venture between Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp, shut down its 35,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit (CDU) on Monday, a company source said.
The company also temporarily stopped the operations of a 16,000-bpd naphtha hydrotreater, a 6,000-bpd platformer and a 14,000-bpd diesel desulphuriser.
"These are all planned maintenance work and there will be no interruption in supply," the source who asked not to be named said.
Caltex has two CDU's which separates crude into components varying from light, medium to heavy distillates and residuals. The other unit has a capacity of 30,000 bpd.
The platformer transforms naphtha into reformates which is a high octane component of gasoline.

On the other hand, the naphtha hydrotreating unit separates sour, whole straight run naphtha into light naphtha used to produce regular gasoline and heavy naphtha used as feed to the platformer to produce reformates.
The diesel desulphuriser removes sulphur content of diesel, the source explained.
Earlier, sources said Caltex also plans to shut for maintenance a 12,000 bpd catalytic cracker next month.

No other information was available concerning the maintenance work on the cracker that produces sour liquefied petroleum gasoline (lpg) and slurry, the heaviest portion which is used for fuel oil production.
